content:
After a long developer and public beta phase, Apple is now rolling out macOS 26.6 to all users with compatible Macs. Here's what the update brings.

macOS 26.6 is now available

macOS 26.6 is now available, addressing over 150 security vulnerabilities, along with other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include correcting the erroneous deprecation notice that incorrectly flagged some apps as Intel-only, and resolving an issue affecting HealthKit and HDR screenshot functionality in Messages.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, macOS 26.6 has likely begun pre-indexing for the new Siri AI, the redesigned Siri app, and other features related to the next generation of Apple Intelligence.

Apple has so far only confirmed this process for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but it appears Macs are going through the same procedure. As users on the macOS 27 beta will know, the indexing process takes several days, so starting it now will help reduce waiting time after upgrading later on.

The release version of macOS 26.6 is build 25G72, which differs from last week's release candidate (25G70).

Spot any other new features in macOS 26.6? Let us know in the comments.
